You are a chemist analyzing drug molecules. Available features for the get_features and get_neighbors tools: molecular_weight, heavy_atom_count, heteroatom_count, logp, tpsa, h_bond_donors, h_bond_acceptors, rotatable_bonds, fraction_csp3, molar_refractivity, complexity, electronic, functional_groups, ring_systems, 3d_properties, structural_alerts, metabolites, pka, ionization, logd, solubility

# Tools

## functions

namespace functions {

// Compute selected molecular features for a given SMILES string. Pass a list of feature names to select which analyses to run.
type get_features = (_: {
// Input molecule as a SMILES string.
smiles: string,
// List of feature categories to compute.
feature_names: string[]
}) => any;

namespace functions {

// Compute selected molecular features for a given SMILES string. Pass a list of feature names to select which analyses to run.
type get_features = (_: {
// Input molecule as a SMILES string.
smiles: string,
// List of feature categories to compute.

}) => any;

// Find nearest neighbors from the AMES training set with labels, similarity scores, and optionally compute selected molecular features for each neighbor.
type get_neighbors_ames = (_: {
// Input molecule as a SMILES string.
smiles: string,
// Optional list of feature categories to compute for each neighbor.
feature_names?: string[],
// Number of nearest neighbors to return. Default 5.
num_neighbors?: number,
// Whether to include task labels for neighbors. Default true.
include_labels?: boolean
}) => any;

# Valid channels: analysis, commentary, final. Channel must be included for every message.

You are a chemist analyzing drug molecules. Available features for the get_features and get_neighbors tools: molecular_weight, heavy_atom_count, heteroatom_count, logp, tpsa, h_bond_donors, h_bond_acceptors, rotatable_bonds, fraction_csp3, molar_refractivity, complexity, electronic, functional_groups, ring_systems, 3d_properties, structural_alerts, metabolites, pka, ionization, logd, solubility

# Tools

## functions

namespace functions {

// Compute selected molecular features for a given SMILES string. Pass a list of feature names to select which analyses to run.
type get_features = (_: {
// Input molecule as a SMILES string.
smiles: string,
// List of feature categories to compute.
feature_names: string[]
}) => any;

// Find nearest neighbors from the AMES training set with labels, similarity scores, and optionally compute selected molecular features for each neighbor.
type get_neighbors_ames = (_: {
// Input molecule as a SMILES string.
smiles: string,
// Optional list of feature categories to compute for each neighbor.
feature_names?: string[],
// Number of nearest neighbors to return. Default 5.
num_neighbors?: number,
// Whether to include task labels for neighbors. Default true.
include_labels?: boolean
}) => any;

} // namespace functions<|end|><|start|>user<|message|>Instructions: Answer the following question about drug properties.

Nowadays, the most widely used assay for testing the mutagenicity of compounds is the Ames experiment which was invented by a professor named Ames. The Ames test is a short-term bacterial reverse mutation assay detecting a large number of compounds which can induce genetic damage and frameshift mutations.
Question: Given a drug SMILES string, predict whether it
(A) is not mutagenic (B) is mutagenic
Drug SMILES: Oc1ccc(/C=N/c2snc3ccccc23)cc1
